column1: # Catalogue numbers whose blurb has been read by hand, and the verdict. Mothli suggests a book that
# is not on the shelf only when its number is here as "clean"; anything not listed is never suggested.
# The rule (the owner's): for unread books use only a spoiler-free blurb. A blurb is "no" if it tells
# how the book ends; who dies, is killed or executed (beyond a death the book opens with); who marries
# or ends up with whom; who a hidden person is or the answer to the mystery; a betrayal or reversal
# kept for late; or, for a sequel, how an earlier book came out. Doubt ("leads to tragedy", "with
# devastating consequences") is "no". Setting, premise, characters at the start, kind and themes are
# "clean". Reasons say what kind of thing is given away, never the thing itself.
# Read on 16 November 2026: 605 blurbs read, 560 clean, 45 no. They are the first
# 601 English books in the catalogue's own order (most read first) after one edition a work, no
# single volumes of a set, a blurb and a genre; and 4 further down (two by Louisa May
# Alcott, two by George Eliot), read for the tests of the author rules. Then the 40 numbers of the
# earlier deny list (15 November 2026, section 6ad of docs/product/companion-audit-2026-11-14.md),
# all no. Non-English books have not been reviewed; every book not listed is never suggested.
# Columns: catalogue number, verdict (clean or no), why (for no).
